title: Plan artifact
description: The contract between the verbs. Plan writes it, apply consumes it and nothing else, verify compares the running instance against it. It is also the artifact a second person reviews and a change request carries, which is why it is safe to share by construction: a secret entry has a name and a location and no field a value could go in.

schema_version.description: The version of this contract. Apply refuses a plan whose major version it does not implement, rather than guessing at a field that moved.

plan_id.description: Derived from the plan's own content, so identical inputs produce an identical id and a plan can be found again by the id printed in a task log.

generated_at.description: UTC, to the second. The only field that legitimately differs between two otherwise identical plans.

version.description: The profile version, not the engine version. It is what lets a value in a six-month-old plan be traced to the rule that produced it.

parameters.description: Every tuned setting, each carrying the rule that produced it and that rule's reasoning. In the order the profile wrote them, which is the order a reviewer reads the rules in; the order they were computed in comes from what they read and is not this one.

configuration.description: Every configuration file apply renders, and where each one lands. Apply reads this rather than the profile, because a plan that does not carry a value apply needs is an incomplete plan.

initialization.description: What creating the instance takes, for an engine whose packages install a server without making one. Absent means installing is all there is to it. This is the one thing apply does that cannot be done again differently, so the plan states it rather than leaving it to a default inside a role: a locale or an encoding chosen here is chosen for the life of the instance, and changing either afterwards means a dump and a reload.

tunables.description: Host settings outside the engine's own configuration that apply sets, each with what it was when the plan was made. An empty list says the engine asks nothing of the host beyond what it installs.

changes.description: Everything apply would do, in the order it would do it. Nothing existing is removed or overwritten, which is why there is no remove action.

secrets.description: The secrets the instance needs, named by where they are stored. There is deliberately nowhere in this object for a value. An empty list says the instance needs none.

version_source.description: Whether a human named the version or the profile default was used. The plan says which, because the two are not the same decision.

arch.description: The processor architecture of the host, as the support matrix spells it.

block.description: A block produces a refusal, never a plan. A plan carrying a block is not a thing that can exist, so the contract says so rather than leaving it to a convention.

skip.description: Rules that could not be evaluated, because the fact they read was not collected or because they did not apply to this host. Counted separately from a pass: a rule nobody could run is not a rule that agreed.

source.description: Where the rule came from, which is where somebody goes to argue with it: the engine-independent rules written in the core, or the ones this profile contributed. A run's results are one list and are resolved on identical terms, so this is a label rather than a difference in standing.

severity.description: How badly the rule matters. There are two severities and there is no third, so a warning cannot be promoted into a refusal, and a refusal cannot be demoted at run time.

outcome.description: What the rule did on this host. A rule of severity block that passes reports pass; one that did not apply reports skip.

value.description: The canonical value: a count of bytes, a number of seconds, a plain number, or the word itself. Not the way a configuration file spells it, which is the engine's own syntax and belongs in the engine's template. Verify reads the running instance back and compares against this, and a comparison of rendered text against whatever a server chose to print is not a comparison.

unit.description: What the value is measured in, so that a reader and a comparison mean the same thing by it.

display.description: The value as a person reads it. It is here so that the diff between two plans is legible: 8589934592 tells a reviewer nothing that 8.0 GiB does not tell them better, and that diff is how a change to a sizing rule gets reviewed.

bounded_by.description: Present when the computed value hit a floor or a ceiling, because a clamped value says something different about the host than one that landed inside its bounds.

above_advisory.description: The threshold this value went past, present only when it did. Permitted, but worth saying out loud. It is not a gate: preflight finished before this parameter existed, so it travels with the parameter and joins the warnings apply has to have acknowledged.

install.description: Package names, resolved for the requested version. Native packages from a vendor repository: nothing here can describe a source build or a tarball.

service.description: The service unit that results, which verify then asserts is enabled and active.

gpg_check.description: Whether the repository's signature is checked. False is a decision that had to survive a code review in the profile, and the plan repeats it so that it survives one here too.

template.description: The template in the profile that renders it.

carries_parameters.description: Whether the sized parameters are written into this file. At most one file may say so, because two would leave nothing to say which one the instance reads them from.

locale.description: The locale the instance is created with, which a shared rule has already proved the host has. Absent means the profile initializes without naming one.

settings.description: Every other choice made while the instance is created, as the engine names them. Apply carries them through to the engine's own role; the core reads none of them.

why.description: A step that cannot be repeated differently without destroying what it made is the step whose reasoning is most worth having in the artifact somebody approves.

observed.description: What the setting was when the plan was made. Absent means the host did not report it, which is a different answer from it being unset, and the change is listed without a from rather than with a guess.

why.description: Changing a setting on somebody else's machine without saying why is how a provisioning tool loses its welcome.

action.description: There is no remove. Apply creates and configures; it does not drop data directories, and it does not overwrite a file without leaving a timestamped copy beside it.

location.description: Where the secret is stored, so that someone can find it. Never the secret.

warnings.description: How many things were said out loud: the warnings preflight raised, plus every parameter that went past a threshold its rule advised against. One count, because there is one acknowledgement, and a warning that arrived after the gates closed is not a lesser warning.

warnings_require_acknowledgement.description: True when the plan carries warnings of either kind. Apply refuses until they are acknowledged explicitly: a warning nobody has to answer for becomes invisible within a month.
